title: Episode 1,000: The Simpsons Spectacular Part II
summary: Episode 1,000 of Stuff You Should Know, part II of a Simpsons tribute. The hosts cover the Simpsons animation production process (writers' room, table read, voice recording, storyboard/story reel, layout, exposure sheets, overseas animation in South Korea), the fictional town of Springfield and its unknown state, the batch-based episode numbering code, Tree House of Horror, couch gags and chalkboard gags, catchphrases like "D'oh" and "Meh," Easter eggs and character trivia, fan-favorite episodes, predictions the show made about real events, and the debate over whether the show declined after its early seasons. The episode closes with tour announcements, a thank-you to listeners, and contact information.

segments.title: Tour announcement and episode 1,000 opening
segments.summary: Chuck announces upcoming tour dates in San Francisco, Seattle and Portland with pre-sale details. Josh and Chuck mark episode 1,000 and tease the second half of the Simpsons tribute.

segments.title: Simpsons production: table read, voice recording and storyboards
segments.summary: After the table read, notes go out and voice actors record separately rather than together. Directors and animators then work from the script. The process runs six to eight months per episode, with overlapping groups working on multiple episodes. Story reel replaces the older storyboard step.

segments.title: Layout, style guide and exposure sheets
segments.summary: Layout is the most finished in-house stage and the longest step, used to refine comedic timing and expressions. The show Bible and style guide keep drawings consistent, such as the nose overlapping the eye and Bart's proportions. Exposure sheets record every frame; at 24 frames per second a 22-minute episode has about 31,680 frames. Frames are then sent overseas, with the South Korean studio Akom doing the final animation.

segments.title: Springfield's unknown location and town details
segments.summary: Springfield is generic on purpose. Matt Groening has said he named it after Springfield, Oregon, though the chalkboard gag says it is in any state but yours. Fans have pointed to clues, such as Ned saying it borders Kentucky, Maine, Nevada and Ohio, and the Lanai Hawaii alternate narration. Running gags include the town's business pun names.

segments.title: Simpsons locations, characters and Ned Flanders' age
segments.summary: The hosts list Springfield landmarks and locations such as Moe's Tavern, the power plant, and Springfield Elementary. Characters do not age. Ned Flanders is said to be sixty years old. A Melanie Griffith audio tour parody at a museum is mentioned.

segments.title: Episode numbering batch codes
segments.summary: Simpsons episodes are numbered by production batch rather than airing order. Early codes used a number and letter, such as 9F03 for season four episode six, and later they switched to letters only, as in AABF09 for season ten episode thirteen. The hosts say they usually identify episodes by title.

segments.title: Couch gags, chalkboard gags and Treehouse of Horror
segments.summary: The show's opening includes the chalkboard gag and the couch gag, which guest animators such as Guillermo del Toro, Don Hertzfeldt, Bill Plympton and Genndy Tartakovsky have created. Maggie's grocery scan price changed from $47.63 to 52 in 2009. Treehouse of Horror is a long-running Halloween tradition parodying horror and sci-fi.

segments.title: Catchphrases: D'oh, Meh and Comic Book Guy's worst episode ever
segments.summary: D'oh is defined in the Oxford English Dictionary and translated in other languages. Meh was added to the OED in 2015. Comic Book Guy's 'worst episode ever' line from the Itchy and Scratchy and Poochie episode is discussed alongside fan criticism and self-referential humor.

segments.title: Predictions the Simpsons made about real events
segments.summary: Time magazine listed ways the show predicted the future. Examples include Siegfried and Roy's tiger attack, the gambling episode, a voting machine glitch in the Treehouse of Horror episode that matches a 2012 election story, Lisa's autocorrect 'beat up Martha' gag, a Trump-related Lisa presidency clip, and an Ebola book seventeen years early.

segments.title: Easter eggs and trivia
segments.summary: Bart's prank call number spells out Smithers. Characters have four fingers, except God. Skinner's prisoner number 2461 is shared with Jean Valjean, Lehman's, Hank Jennings and Bob. Michael Jackson was an uncredited guest and co-producer of Bartman. Millhouse's middle name is Mussolini. Cletus's children have names like Normal Head Joe. A Happy Days line is discussed.

segments.title: Best episodes lists and Homer Backward Are
segments.summary: The hosts compare best-episode lists from Rolling Stone, Digital Spy, IGN, Entertainment Weekly, Consequence of Sound and Vulture, naming episodes like Marge Versus the Monorail, Homer the Heretic, Cape Fear and Homer Backward Are. Matt Groening's personal top ten is mentioned. Homer Backward Are is linked to Flowers for Algernon.

segments.title: Simpsons decline debate, satire and cultural impact
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether the show declined after season eight or ten, the 'Zombie Simpsons' idea, and fan fragmentation. They discuss George H.W. Bush's remark that he wanted America to be more like the Waltons, Barbara Bush's criticism, Bill Cosby's 1990 comments on TV, and the difficulty of satire today. They argue the show's core is morality, and mention shows like Master of None and One Mississippi.

segments.title: Thanks, listener contact and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners, mention the listener mail segment and contact channels (Twitter, Facebook, email at stuffpodcast@howstuffworks.com), and sign off.
